amendment.oldTarget: gh commands time out after 120 seconds (decided with the user; the daemon is expected to become multi-threaded so a slow gh will not block it). The approval wait has its own timeout, set in s3's LLD. Conversion is serial, so a text-only tool that needs the cheap model costs one model call per attempt plus at most one escalated call; structured-output tools make no model call.
amendment.newTarget: Each gh job has its own time limit from a table keyed by tool id and op, never shorter than the tool has today: reads 30 s (gh_pr_diff and gh_run_view 60 s, searches 60 s), changes 30 s by default, gh_issue_create 60 s, gh_pr_create 90 s, gh_pr_merge and gh_release_create 180 s, gh_repo_create and gh_repo_fork 120 s, downloads and uploads 300 s, gh_repo_clone 600 s, codespace create and rebuild 600 s (decided with the user on 2026-10-25; the daemon is expected to become multi-threaded so a slow gh will not block it). A timed-out call names the command and the limit, and a changing call adds that its outcome is unknown. The approval wait has its own timeout, set in s3's LLD. Conversion is serial, so a text-only tool that needs the cheap model costs one model call per attempt plus at most one escalated call; structured-output tools make no model call.
amendment.rationale: Decided with the user in chat on 2026-10-25 (docs/plans/tool-registry.md, s5 decisions): one 120 s line shortens a clone or a codespace create and over-allows a plain read, so the limit follows the job.

body.rationale: Records the user decision of 2026-10-25 that the gh time limit follows the job; Story s5 built it (ghTimeoutMs in src/daemon/tools/builtins/gh/helpers.ts and the limits of each op).
